approachQuestion.prompt:
Kth distinct score

Return the kth largest DISTINCT value in an integer array, or report absent if fewer than k distinct values exist. k≥1. 1≤n≤200000; signed 32-bit values. Examples: [8,8,5,2], k=2→5; [4,4], k=2→absent.

Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method that returns the required result for every allowed input.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.

options.text: Sort descending and count a value only when it differs from the previous value; stop at distinct rank k.
options.feedback: Skipping equal runs makes rank count distinct values.

options.text: Sort descending and return position k−1.
options.feedback: Duplicates shift the rank: [8,8,5], k=2 returns 8 instead of 5.

options.text: Return the kth smallest array element.
options.feedback: This reverses the requested rank direction.

options.text: For each distinct candidate value, count the number of DISTINCT array values larger than it; return the candidate whose count is k−1.
options.feedback: This correctly determines distinct rank, but rebuilding a distinct list and recounting it for every candidate repeats work that one sort and run scan avoids.

feedback.reason: The kth distinct score is the beginning of the kth value run, not the kth array position.
details: Comparison-sort descending, skip repeated values, and stop when the kth distinct run begins.
The kth distinct score is the beginning of the kth value run, not the kth array position. Duplicate submissions must advance within a run without incrementing the distinct counter.
“Sort descending and count a value only when it differs from the previous value; stop at distinct rank k.”: Skipping equal runs makes rank count distinct values.
“Sort descending and return position k−1.”: Duplicates shift the rank: [8,8,5], k=2 returns 8 instead of 5.
“Return the kth smallest array element.”: This reverses the requested rank direction.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed below, choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count working copies, event/heap/visited storage and sort buffers; exclude the caller input and returned output. Comparisons and arithmetic take constant time; merge sort uses a linear buffer.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

details: Sorting the entire copied score array happens before choosing distinct runs, so even a small requested k does not remove its O(n log n) cost. Skipping duplicates adds at most O(n). Copy and merge buffer require O(n) auxiliary space; no scan over score pairs creates a quadratic factor.
